title: NL Palette
one_liner: A command palette for a Markdown editor that understands what you mean, re-ranked on every keystroke pause, with a 30-case live benchmark against fzf-style fuzzy.
what_it_does: The page is a working Markdown notes editor with sidebar, tabs, outline, four themes, zoom, preview, zen mode and 66 commands. The user presses Ctrl/Cmd+K and types plain English such as "make this louder" or "get rid of the sidebar". After a 100 ms debounce the app sends {query, app_state} to a Node proxy, which asks Jev six questions in one call: which command (choice over 66 ids), four speculative argument slots (font delta, theme, heading level, export format) and one noul "is this destructive". Stale in-flight requests abort. The list re-ranks by command probability with a live probability bar, and the top row shows an argument preview like "Change Font Size by +2 pt". A confidence gate at 0.55 controls Enter: above it Enter runs the top item; below it the top-3 show dashed and Enter needs an explicit arrow or hover pick. Destructive commands or is_destructive >= 0.5 open a confirm dialog. Tab cycles Jev / side-by-side / fuzzy-only modes; the footer shows session p50/p95 latency measured with performance.now(). A Benchmark panel runs 30 phrasings through both approaches with concurrency 8 and shows accuracy@1, argument accuracy, mean/p50/p95 latency, elapsed and queries/s (Jev 100% vs fuzzy 20%).

jev_questions.instructions: {task: "The user typed `query` into the command palette of a Markdown notes editor. Which editor command do they want to run?", notes: ["Match on meaning, not on exact words; users describe the effect they want.", "`app_state` describes the editor right now. A request to hide something that is visible, or show something that is hidden, means the toggle for that thing.", "Requests about text size mean the editor font size; requests about the whole window or interface being bigger/smaller mean zoom."]}
options: 66 command ids from src/shared/commands.ts, criterion = `${title}: ${description}` each, e.g. toggle_sidebar, toggle_outline, toggle_status_bar, toggle_minimap, toggle_line_numbers, toggle_word_wrap, toggle_preview, toggle_zen_mode, toggle_fullscreen, zoom_in, zoom_out, reset_zoom, split_editor, close_split, set_theme, change_font_size, reset_font_size, toggle_ligatures, cycle_font_family, toggle_typewriter_mode, set_heading, toggle_bold, toggle_italic, toggle_strikethrough, toggle_inline_code, insert_code_block, toggle_bullet_list, toggle_numbered_list, toggle_task_list, toggle_blockquote, insert_link, insert_image, insert_table, insert_horizontal_rule, insert_date, clear_formatting, uppercase_selection, lowercase_selection, title_case_selection, sort_lines, remove_duplicate_lines, trim_trailing_whitespace, join_lines, duplicate_line, delete_line, move_line_up, move_line_down, undo, redo, select_all, find, find_replace, go_to_line, toggle_spell_check, new_note, save_note, export_note, rename_note, delete_note, toggle_pin_note, close_tab, close_other_tabs, reopen_closed_tab, next_tab, previous_tab, toggle_autosave
jev_questions.state_shape: {query: string (<=300 chars), app_state: {sidebar_visible, outline_visible, preview_visible, zen_mode: boolean, theme: string, font_size: number, zoom_percent: number, selection_exists: boolean, open_tabs: number, word_wrap, line_numbers, spell_check, autosave: boolean}}

jev_questions.instructions: If the user is asking to change the text or font size, by how many points and in which direction? Small nudges are 2 points; 'a lot', 'much', or 'way' bigger/smaller is 4 points. Making text bigger, larger, louder or more readable is positive; smaller, tinier or more compact is negative.
options: -4: Much smaller text: shrink the font by 4 points
-2: Slightly smaller text: shrink the font by 2 points
+2: Slightly bigger text: grow the font by 2 points
+4: Much bigger text: grow the font by 4 points

jev_questions.instructions: If the user is asking to change the color theme, which theme do they want? Night, black or dim means dark; day, bright or white means light; warm, paper or vintage means sepia; accessibility or maximum readability means high contrast. If they just want a different look than the current `app_state.theme`, pick the most common alternative (dark when currently light, light otherwise).
options: dark: Dark theme: dark background, light text (night mode)
light: Light theme: white background, dark text (day mode)
sepia: Sepia theme: warm cream paper-like background
high_contrast: High contrast theme: black and yellow for maximum legibility

jev_questions.instructions: If the user is asking to make a heading, which level? Title, top, biggest or main heading is 1; section or subheading is 2; subsection is 3. Words like 'h4', 'level 5', 'smallest heading' name the level directly.

If the user is asking to export or download the note, which file format do they want? A printable or shareable document is PDF; a web page is HTML; raw text without markup is plain text; keeping the .md source is Markdown.
options: pdf: PDF document for printing or sharing
plain_text: Plain text (.txt) with all markup stripped

jev_questions.instructions: Does the user's `query` ask for something that would permanently discard content or close work (deleting a note, deleting lines, closing tabs)? criteria.true: The request removes, deletes, discards or closes something for good. criteria.false: The request only shows, changes, formats, navigates or can be trivially undone.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text": "Editor state: sidebar visible, outline hidden, preview hidden, theme light, font 14pt, zoom 100%, no selection, 3 tabs, word wrap on, line numbers on, spell check on.\nUser typed in the command palette: \"get rid of the sidebar\"", "labels": {"toggle_sidebar": "Toggle Sidebar: Show or hide the left-hand file explorer panel (the sidebar with the note list).", "toggle_outline": "Toggle Outline Panel: Show or hide the document outline of headings on the right.", ... one entry per command, `${title}: ${description}` ...}} -> {label, probability, confidence, scores:{id: score}}. Rank = scores sorted desc, top 8. Gate = probability >= 0.55.
dm1_mapping.notes: classify caps labels at 64; there are 66 commands. Drop toggle_fullscreen (cannot work inside the page anyway) and toggle_ligatures to reach 64, or use classify-tree with the 10 groups as level 1 and commands as level 2 (keeps all 66, but only the chosen group gets level-2 scores, so cross-group top-8 ranking is lost). Recommend the 64-label classify. The Jev notes about app_state and text-size-vs-zoom go into the text prefix and into label descriptions (zoom_in: "...whole interface, not the text size").

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text": "<same text as command>", "labels": {"-4": "Much smaller text: shrink the font by 4 points (a lot, way, much smaller)", "-2": "Slightly smaller text: shrink the font by 2 points", "+2": "Slightly bigger text: grow the font by 2 points (bigger, larger, louder, more readable)", "+4": "Much bigger text: grow the font by 4 points (a lot, way, much bigger)"}}
dm1_mapping.notes: Fire only when the top command is change_font_size, chained after the command result. Not speculative like Jev.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text": "<same text as command>", "labels": {"dark": "Dark theme: dark background, light text (night, black, dim)", "light": "Light theme: white background, dark text (day, bright, white)", "sepia": "Sepia theme: warm cream paper-like background (warm, paper, vintage)", "high_contrast": "High contrast theme: black and yellow for maximum legibility (accessibility, readable)"}}
dm1_mapping.notes: Fire only when top command is set_theme. The 'different look than current theme' rule: handle in code, if query has no theme word and scores are flat, pick dark when app_state.theme is light, else light.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text": "<same text as command>", "labels": {"1": "Heading level 1, H1, the largest: title, top, biggest or main heading", "2": "Heading level 2, H2: section or subheading", "3": "Heading level 3, H3: subsection", "4": "Heading level 4, H4", "5": "Heading level 5, H5", "6": "Heading level 6, H6, the smallest heading"}}
dm1_mapping.notes: Fire only when top command is set_heading.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text": "<same text as command>", "labels": {"markdown": "Markdown (.md) source file, keep the source", "html": "HTML web page", "pdf": "PDF document for printing or sharing", "plain_text": "Plain text (.txt) with all markup stripped, raw text"}}
dm1_mapping.notes: Fire only when top command is export_note.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"text": "<same text as command>", "statement": "The request permanently discards content or closes work.", "when_true": "The request removes, deletes, discards or closes something for good.", "when_false": "The request only shows, changes, formats, navigates or can be trivially undone."} -> {answer, probability}. wantsConfirmation = command.destructive || probability >= 0.5.
dm1_mapping.notes: Do not fire per keystroke. Fire once on Enter before executing, only when the chosen command is not already flagged destructive. Skip it entirely for commands flagged destructive (already confirm).

browser_plan: Same shape as the original: a Vite/React page on demo.milliseconds.ai/nl-palette with the real editor, Ctrl/Cmd+K palette, side-by-side fuzzy mode and Benchmark panel. Copy editor/, shared/commands.ts, fuzzy.ts, stats.ts, data/benchmark.ts as-is. Replace server/jev.ts + server/index.ts with one proxy route (Cloudflare Worker or Node) that forwards POST /api/dm1/:route to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/:route with the bearer key, passes through x-inference-ms and x-input-tokens headers, and returns 429 as-is. Client: build one text string from app_state + query, POST /classify with 64 described labels. Debounce 250 ms (not 100), abort stale requests, and add a client-side gate of one in-flight request plus a minimum 500 ms spacing between sends (about 2 req/s). Rank from scores, gate at probability >= 0.55, argument preview from a chained second classify only when the top command has an arg slot (change_font_size, set_theme, set_heading, export_note). Destructive check: one yes-no on Enter. On HTTP 429 show a 'Rate limited, retrying' pill, back off using retry-after, keep the last ranking visible, and fall back to fuzzy results labeled FUZZY. Benchmark: one POST /classify with texts: [30 prefixed queries] (one request, 30 results), then four batched arg calls (texts of the 2 font, 2 theme, 2 heading, 2 export cases) = 5 requests total instead of 30. Compute accuracy@1, arg accuracy, and latency from x-inference-ms plus performance.now(). Fuzzy baseline runs in the browser unchanged. Style with the milliseconds.ai tokens from ~/projects/cloudraker-spring-2026 instead of styles.css; keep the four editor themes as scoped CSS variables inside the editor pane.
risks: classify limit of 64 labels vs 66 commands: must drop or merge 2 commands, or use classify-tree and lose cross-group ranking.
No state field in DM1: app_state must be prose in the text; disambiguation (hide vs show, text size vs zoom) depends on label descriptions and may be weaker than Jev's structured notes.
Latency: the demo needs a full round trip well under 300 ms for search-as-you-type feel; two chained calls (command + arg) double that on arg commands.
Rate limit is org-wide (200 req/min): several concurrent visitors typing will hit 429; the client throttle helps but cannot prevent it, so fuzzy fallback and the 429 pill are required.
Benchmark accuracy will differ from the README's 100% claim; the page must show measured numbers, not the Jev figures.
Speculative arg slots are gone: the arg preview appears one request later than the ranking.
Fuzzy scorer and editor executor are large (143 + 375 lines) but pure; port risk is low, styling risk is moderate (771 lines of CSS to re-theme).
